canonical.description: The surface is settled and usable with its primary content present.
Content the surface needs has been requested and has not arrived yet.
A user-initiated mutation is in flight and its outcome is not yet known.
A change is being persisted, typically without the user having pressed a submit control.
Local and remote state are being reconciled in the background.
Usable content is already shown while newer content is being fetched.
The request succeeded and there is legitimately nothing to show.
The primary task is usable while some supporting content is unavailable.
Content is shown but is known to be out of date and its freshness affects decisions.
An operation completed and the surface is acknowledging it before settling.
User-supplied input was rejected and the user can correct it in place.
An operation failed for a reason outside the user's input and may be retryable.
The operation is understood and refused because the actor is not authorized.
Connectivity is unavailable; some behavior is degraded or queued.
A previously failed operation is being attempted again.

groups.description: The settled state a surface returns to; the destination of every recovery path.
Work is in flight. Distinguished by who started it and whether prior content remains visible.
The request resolved but the content itself is absent, incomplete, or aged.
A momentary acknowledgement that an operation finished, before settling back to resting.
Something failed. Distinguished by whether the user can fix it in place.
An explicit second attempt following a fault.

region-lifecycle.description: The projection used by scenario-experience-spec RegionLifecycle.states, which governs whether a declared async region is settled.

excluded.name: static
excluded.reason: Not a state. It describes whether the region resolves asynchronously at all, which RegionLifecycle already carries on its `kind` field — the enum listing it as a state is redundant and should be removed in the next spec minor.

request-lifecycle.description: The projection DESIGN.md describes in prose under Request Lifecycle, for the states of a single network call or long-running task.

excluded.name: disabled
excluded.reason: Not a state of the surface. It is a property of an individual control, expressible through the element's own accessible state rather than through the page or component state axis.

design-required.description: The floor a scenario's DESIGN.md is expected to require of every page. Replaces the hardcoded allowlist in checks/state_coverage.go, whose DESIGN.md section parser matched no file in the repo and therefore never produced a finding.

excluded.name: disabled
excluded.reason: Same reason as request-lifecycle: a control property, not a surface state. Carrying it in a page-level required list made the list unsatisfiable in principle.
